summary: This is a Docusaurus plugin that generates RSS 2.0 feeds from blog posts. It creates a main site-wide feed at /blog/rss.xml, plus optional per-tag and per-series feeds so readers can subscribe to specific topics. The plugin extracts article content from built HTML files, cleans up UI elements, converts relative URLs to absolute ones, and optionally includes post images and author information.

explanations.71: This function joins URL path parts using forward slashes (POSIX style) and ensures the result always starts with a slash—so 'blog' + 'tags' becomes '/blog/tags'.
explanations.83: This assembles a complete absolute URL by combining the site's base URL (like 'https://example.com/') with a relative path, handling edge cases like trailing slashes.
explanations.95: This looks at a file extension (from a URL like 'image.png') and returns the proper MIME type that RSS feeds need to describe what kind of file it is.
explanations.120: This sanitizes text to remove characters that would break XML parsers—things like non-breaking spaces and control characters that aren't visible but cause parsing errors.
explanations.144: This merges three sets of CSS selectors: ones that are always removed (like headers and SVGs), defaults the plugin defines, and any the user added—so unwanted elements get stripped from RSS content.
explanations.150: This reads the built HTML file for a blog post, parses it with cheerio (like jQuery for Node), finds the article content, removes unwanted elements based on selectors, and returns clean HTML safe for RSS.
explanations.163: This tries multiple strategies to find the main article container in the HTML: first looks for an <article> tag, then falls back to Docusaurus theme classes if that didn't work.
explanations.179: This finds Docusaurus's code block wrappers and simplifies them—it extracts just the actual code container and discards the outer wrapper so the RSS feed looks cleaner.
explanations.196: This computes a slug (URL-friendly identifier) for a post by either using a slug defined in front matter or deriving one from the file path and normalizing it to lowercase with hyphens.
explanations.231: This groups feed items by their tags, including both explicitly declared tags and the post's 'mainTag', using a per-post 'seen' set to avoid adding the same post twice if a tag appears in both places.
explanations.236: This normalizes the tags field (which might be a string, array, or undefined) into an array so the rest of the code can treat it consistently.
explanations.269: This groups feed items by their series field from front matter, computing a slug for each series the same way the series route plugin does—so the feed URL sits next to the series page.
explanations.311: This is the core function that builds one complete RSS 2.0 XML document; it takes a Feed object, channel metadata, items, and config options, then uses cheerio to inject author names into the XML after the feed library generates it.
explanations.322: This creates a new RSS feed object with channel metadata like title and description; the 'updated' date is deliberately set to the newest post's date rather than 'now' to avoid rewriting the entire file on every build when nothing changed.
explanations.344: This array stores author markup as XML strings because the feed library doesn't natively support the 'dc:creator' element with CDATA sections—it will be injected into the serialized XML later.
explanations.405: This spread operator conditionally adds an 'enclosure' object to the feed item only if images are enabled and an image URL and MIME type exist; it's a clean way to add optional RSS elements.
explanations.417: This calls the feed library's method to serialize all the items added so far into an RSS 2.0 XML string.
explanations.424: This loads the serialized RSS XML string into cheerio in XML mode so it can be parsed and modified like HTML—specifically to inject 'dc:creator' elements that the feed library doesn't support natively.
explanations.427: This adds the Dublin Core namespace declaration to the root <rss> element so XML parsers know that 'dc:creator' tags are valid.
explanations.440: This loop matches each generated XML item with its corresponding author markup by position—the feed library outputs items in the same order they were added, so index-based matching is safe.
explanations.452: This replaces the default XML declaration with a custom one that also includes a reference to a stylesheet (rss.xsl)—the URL is absolute so it works from any feed location, not just /blog/.
explanations.481: This dynamically imports the 'feed' package inside the postBuild hook so it only loads when actually needed, avoiding top-level dependency issues.
explanations.506: This parses the authors.yml file (YAML format) into a JavaScript object so author keys from post front matter can be looked up to get full author details like names.
explanations.516: This optionally loads tag metadata (labels and descriptions) from tags.yml; if the file doesn't exist, it defaults to an empty object so the code doesn't crash.
explanations.525: This runs an async operation on every blog post file in parallel: read it, extract front matter metadata, filter out drafts/unlisted posts, and compute the permalink.
explanations.539: This gets the post's publish date from front matter if present; otherwise it falls back to the file's birth time (creation date) from the file system.
explanations.564: This fetches the full rendered HTML body for each post by calling getArticleHtml, which reads the built HTML file and extracts the article content—this is expensive so it happens in parallel.
explanations.576: This filters posts to only those marked as published (not explicitly false) and that have actual content, then sorts them newest first so the feed shows recent posts at the top.
explanations.584: This takes the first N published posts (up to maxItems) for the site-wide feed, using Math.max to ensure at least one item even if maxItems is somehow invalid.
explanations.613: This early return skips per-topic feed generation if the user set emitTopicFeeds to false, saving processing time when only a main feed is wanted.
explanations.644: This skips creating a tag feed if it would have fewer posts than minPostsPerTagFeed (default 1), preventing empty or thin feeds for tags that rarely appear.
explanations.683: This caps the number of items in each topic feed to topicMaxItems (default 10) because topic feeds carry descriptions only (not full content), so they're smaller and faster to generate and subscribe to.
